structured.approach: I read the TSK-07 definition in feat.tasks to see what the Frontend task needs: a pure render function in ap_portal with no transport layer. I took the granted secrets from the tool view, which reflects the restricted permission table; I referred to that table only and did not quote it. To check that nothing in the repository needs a secret, I read package.json and ci.mjs and searched the repository for environment-variable and secret-like names (case-insensitive). Required secrets (none) match granted secrets (none), so I raised no access request. I wrote task.secrets_scope with secret names only and no values.

claims.text: The Frontend task in scope is TSK-07 for STORY-07 in ap_portal. It adds renderOverdueRisk(rows) in src/ap_portal/index.js, a version step in package.json and tests in tests/portal.test.js. It depends only on the CT-1 field list.
TSK-06 adds no transport layer, so the portal function only receives rows as an argument and needs no network credentials.
The permission table grants no secrets to ap_portal and none are required.
package.json declares no dependencies and only the ci script `node ci.mjs`; the version is 2.3.0.
ci.mjs sets only NODE_PATH to 'src' in the environment and reads no secret variable.
The repository uses Node.js 22 CommonJS with node:test.
TSK-08 end-to-end harness belongs to the Testing Agent and uses a synthetic feed only, outside the Frontend secrets scope.

structured.summary: TSK-07 (STORY-07, ap_portal) needs no secrets in local/CI, dev or main, and the permission table grants none for the repository. They match, so I raised no access request and found no excess access. Repository checks back this up: package.json has no dependencies, and ci.mjs only sets NODE_PATH. task.secrets_scope.md is written with secret names only (here, none). There are no open questions.
